Halifax Text Not Arriving? Bank Verification Code Fixes

A missing Halifax or bank passcode is usually a delivery or account-verification problem, not proof of a scam. Run these checks once, then contact the bank safely.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-05-07 · Updated 2026-08-01 · 5 min read

Quick answer: A missing bank passcode is usually a delivery or account problem, not proof of fraud or a SIM swap. Check signal, blocked-message folders and that the bank holds your current mobile number, then request one fresh code. If it still fails, contact the bank through its official app or the number on your card.
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Use the right recovery route. Follow the payment, account and identity checklist; reporting differs in Scotland.

First identify which bank text is missing

A single missing bank code can have several possible causes and is not proof of fraud or a SIM swap — start with the normal delivery and account checks below. Banks send different kinds of messages: one-time passcodes for a payment or login, security checks, and optional account alerts. Confirm which message you expected and whether the bank still has your current mobile number. Do not keep requesting codes repeatedly; use one fresh request after completing the checks below.

Run these low-risk checks first

Check that the phone has signal and Airplane Mode is off, restart it, and look in blocked, filtered or junk-message folders. Confirm that the inbox has space and that you can receive an ordinary text or call from someone you know. Then request one new code and wait for the newest message; older codes may expire when a replacement is issued. Menu names vary, so use the phone manufacturer's official help if you cannot find a setting.

Halifax text messages not arriving: the relevant checks

Check that Halifax has your current mobile number — it needs this to send passcodes, and extra security checks may use an app, an SMS passcode or a phone call depending on the task and account. Halifax is transitioning its brand to Lloyds and says customers who have moved will approve Halifax-card payments in the Lloyds app, so type halifax.co.uk yourself and follow the current instructions shown for your account rather than assuming which branded app applies. If you cannot complete the check, contact the bank through the official app or the number printed on your card.

This is a service-access problem; the separate Fake Halifax Text? Scam Checks, 159 and Safe Reporting guide covers unexpected messages claiming to be Halifax.

Check the bank account and mobile number

Sign in through the bank's official app or a website address you typed yourself. Check that the registered mobile number is correct, including after a recent number change, new SIM or account update. Look for an in-app notice about maintenance or a security hold. If the app offers another verification route, follow only the instructions shown inside the official app; availability differs by bank and transaction.

Contact the bank without using a message link

If other calls and texts arrive but only the bank message is missing, contact the bank through its official app or the number printed on your card. Ask it to confirm the registered number, whether the attempted action generated a code, and which alternative verification methods are available for your account. Do not use a support number from a search advert, unexpected text or caller.

When it may be a bank or network delivery issue

Check the bank's official service-status or help page, then ask the bank and mobile provider whether they can see a current delivery problem — don't diagnose the cause from social-media posts alone. SMS passes through systems operated by the sender, messaging suppliers and mobile networks, so a delay can occur outside your phone; the NCSC advises organisations to understand and audit that supply chain because message content, sender details and delivery can be affected.

Separate a missing code from possible SIM-swap warning signs

A missing bank code alone does not establish a SIM swap. The NCSC describes SIM-swap attacks as an attacker transferring a victim's number to another SIM so the attacker can receive calls and messages intended for that number — make urgent checks if you also notice unexpected loss of normal calls and SMS, an unrecognised mobile-account or number-port change, or unauthorised financial activity; these are escalation prompts, not a definitive diagnostic list.

What to do if there are SIM-swap warning signs

Use another phone or a secure internet connection to contact the mobile network and bank through official routes. Ask the network whether a SIM replacement or number port was requested, ask the bank to protect the account, and secure the email account used for recovery. Keep records of alerts and unauthorised changes. Report suspected fraud to Report Fraud in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or to Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland. Do not describe a routine bank-code delay as a confirmed SIM swap.

Frequently asked questions

Why is my bank verification text not arriving?

Check signal, Airplane Mode, blocked or filtered messages, and whether the bank has your current mobile number. Request one fresh code. If ordinary calls and texts work but the bank code still does not arrive, contact the bank through its app or the number on your card.

Why are my Halifax text messages not arriving?

Halifax says it needs your up-to-date mobile number to send a passcode and may use an app, SMS or phone call for extra checks. It is transitioning customers to the Lloyds brand, so follow the current instructions shown at halifax.co.uk or in your account rather than assuming which app applies. Contact the bank through the official app or the number on your card if the check still fails.

Does a missing bank code mean my SIM was swapped?

No. A missing code alone has several routine explanations. Contact the network and bank urgently if the phone also loses service, ordinary calls and texts stop, or you discover a SIM replacement or number-port request you did not make.

How do I know whether a bank text is genuine?

A familiar sender name or message thread is not proof because SMS origin information can be imitated. Do not use an unexpected link or share a code with a caller. Open the bank's app yourself or call the number on your card; forward a suspicious text to 7726.

  • Pause before sending money or credentials
  • Verify with an official site, app, or number
  • Never share one-time passcodes
  • Be sceptical of bank transfer pressure
